input: Schedule a property valuation before listing

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this is a single property or multiple, and whether sale or rental listing, changes the type and number of valuations needed.
Knowing whether the user already has a preferred agent or valuer in mind, or needs help identifying one, determines how much of the sourcing work the plan must cover.
The property's location affects which local valuers or agents are relevant and how quickly appointments can be arranged.
The target listing date creates a hard deadline that dictates how urgently the valuation must be booked.
Whether the user wants a formal RICS/independent surveyor valuation or an informal agent appraisal changes who to contact and what the output looks like.
Knowing who needs to be present at the property (owner, tenant, agent) and access arrangements determines the coordination steps required.
Understanding what a successful valuation outcome looks like — e.g. a written report, a price range, mortgage-ready certificate — ensures the right type of valuer is booked.

gold.taskTitle: Schedule a property valuation before listing
gold.taskDescription: Arrange a professional property valuation appointment ahead of putting the property on the market for sale or rent.

questions.title: Are you listing this property for sale or for rent?
questions.description: Determines the type of valuation required — market sale appraisal vs. rental appraisal — and which professionals to approach.

questions.title: Do you already have a valuer or agent in mind?
questions.description: Establishes whether the plan needs to include sourcing and comparing valuers, or can jump straight to booking.

questions.title: What city or area is the property located in?
questions.description: Location determines which local agents or certified surveyors are available and how competitive the market context is.

questions.title: When are you aiming to have the property listed?
questions.description: The target listing date sets the deadline and urgency for booking the valuation appointment.

questions.title: Do you need a formal surveyor report or an agent appraisal?
questions.description: Distinguishes between a formal RICS-certified valuation (e.g. for mortgage or legal purposes) and an informal estate agent pricing appraisal.

questions.title: Who needs to be present to give access on the day?
questions.description: Identifies whether coordinating with a tenant, co-owner, or property manager is needed as part of the scheduling steps.

questions.title: What output do you need from the valuation appointment?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the user needs a written report, a verbal price estimate, a mortgage-ready certificate, or simply a listing price recommendation.
